hints: Look at the job of each cell and ask, which one needs to make, package and release a lot of product? That job needs lots of packaging organelles.
Recall which organelles have one membrane (rough ER, Golgi body, vesicles, lysosomes) versus two membranes (nucleus, mitochondrion) versus none (ribosomes, cilia microtubules).
walkthrough:
**Sort organelles by membranes**

Think like a biologist first. Single membrane structures include rough and smooth endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi body, secretory vesicles, lysosomes and vacuoles.

Double membrane structures are the nucleus and mitochondria. Non-membrane structures include ribosomes, centrioles, cilia and cytoskeleton.

**Link each cell to its job**

A ciliated cell needs many mitochondria for energy and many non-membrane cilia for movement. A smooth muscle cell needs many mitochondria and myofilaments for contraction. A mature red blood cell has lost its nucleus and mitochondria to carry more haemoglobin.

A goblet cell is a secretory cell. Its whole job is to make, process and release mucus by exocytosis.

**Pick the secretory specialist**

To secrete mucus, a goblet cell is packed full of rough ER to make protein, Golgi body to modify it, and hundreds of mucus-filled secretory vesicles waiting at the top of the cell.

All of those are single-membrane structures, so the goblet cell has the highest proportion of them. Answer B is correct.

options.A: Ciliated cells have many mitochondria (double membrane) and cilia (no membrane), so single-membrane structures are not dominant.
options.B: Goblet cells secrete mucus and are filled with rough ER, Golgi body and secretory vesicles, all of which are bound by a single membrane.
options.C: Mature red blood cells have no nucleus, no mitochondria and no ER, they contain mainly haemoglobin and cell surface membrane.
options.D: Smooth muscle cells need mitochondria for ATP and protein filaments for contraction, not a large secretory system of single-membrane vesicles.
